messages:
Maya: Heads-up — a customer reported confusing errors when requests hit a fallback model. Console shows 422 and the SDK surfaces a retry hint, but backend logs show a capacity fallback (should be 429-ish).
Thomas: ugh. Can you paste the exact payload/logs?
Maya: pasted stack + sample response below. Note the headers.
Maya: HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
Maya: Content-Type: application/json
Maya: X-Redwood-Fallback: model-variant:babbage-quant
Maya: X-Redwood-Route: nl-gen-04
Maya: X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 0
Maya: {"error":"validation_failed","message":"prompt flagged"}
Rachel: So two problems: (1) incorrect status code for a fallback/capacity/quota situation, (2) no structured telemetry that ties the console badge to the exact fallback reason. Both will confuse customers.
Samir: Agree. We should split internal error tags (validation, fallback, capacity) from client-facing status and hint. Right now validation loses the context of quota==0 header.
Jun: Proposal: map these to a small taxonomy exposed to clients via headers + a single canonical HTTP status. Eg: 429 for rate/quota/capacity; 400/422 for strict schema/validation; 503 for degraded/unavailable. Add X-Redwood-Error-Class: FALLBACK|VALIDATION|DEGRADED.
Emily: +1. Also add X-Redwood-Retry-After/Hint for 429 and X-Redwood-Fallback-Used for visibility.
Thomas: For telemetry: we need fields in logs/metrics that the console can query: route_id, model_variant, fallback_reason, tenant_quota_pct, fallback_count. That lets dashboard show "fallback rate" and link to traces.
Maya: Customers asked for actionable console copy. Example UX: show badge "Degraded — using fallback model" with tooltip: "Latency or capacity constraints caused a model variant fallback; some responses may be lower-fidelity. See details and retry/limit guidance."
Rachel: We should also attach a concise runbook link and a button: "Request capacity" (route to sales/ops flow) — enterprise only.
Samir: Edge case: validation failures that coincide with zero quota. Do we prefer to return 429 with a subcode X-Redwood-Error-Subcode: VALIDATION_WHEN_QUOTA? That could be confusing. Better to surface both: status 422 + header X-Redwood-Error-Class: FALLBACK and X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 0. Client SDK can prefer the header for retry logic.
Jun: Hmm. I lean to using status for client-expected behavior (retry/no-retry) and headers for machine-readable hints. So if quota==0 -> 429. If validation-only -> 422. If both, 429 + headers explaining validation block as a secondary signal.
Emily: We'll need to update SDKs to prefer the header X-Redwood-Error-Class for machine decisions, and keep status for quick user-level branching. Add testcases to the SDK test harness.
Maya: Action items:
Maya: 1) eng-platform: agree on canonical mapping table (status vs header) — owner: Thomas — due EOD Fri
Maya: 2) eng-runtime: emit new headers (Error-Class, Fallback-Used, Quota-Remaining, Route-ID) — owner: Samir — due next Tue
Maya: 3) devex: SDK change to read Error-Class first for retry logic + doc copy update — owner: Emily — PR queue next week
Maya: 4) product/console: new badge text + telemetry panel for fallback rate + runbook link — owner: Rachel — prototype by next sync
Thomas: I'll sketch mapping now:
Thomas: VALIDATION -> 400/422, X-Redwood-Error-Class: VALIDATION, Retry: no
Thomas: QUOTA/CAPACITY/FALLBACK -> 429, X-Redwood-Error-Class: FALLBACK, X-Redwood-Fallback-Used: true, Retry: depends (Retry-After header)
Thomas: DEGRADED (auto-degrade due to infra) -> 503, X-Redwood-Error-Class: DEGRADED, Retry: maybe with backoff
Samir: Adding a sample response for the fallback case we should emit: 
Samir: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Samir: Content-Type: application/json
Samir: X-Redwood-Error-Class: FALLBACK
Samir: X-Redwood-Fallback-Used: model-variant:babbage-quant
Samir: X-Redwood-Route: nl-gen-04
Samir: X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining: 0
Samir: X-Redwood-Retry-After: 30
Samir: {"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"tenant token exhausted for route"}
Emily: Good. For telemetry naming conventions, use snake_case for headers and dot-separated metric tags in metrics (route.id, fallback.used, tenant.quota_pct).
Rachel: UX note: console should surface a timeline showing when fallbacks started and the percent of requests affected; also add a quick link to the example request in traces.
DevOpsBot: Canary rollout for header changes scheduled at 2026-03-22T02:00Z. Notifying eng-runtime on-call.
Maya: Thanks. If everyone is aligned I'll consolidate the mapping table and create a small RFC doc + sample dashboard mock.
Thomas: I can take the RFC stub.
Maya: assigning to Thomas, Samir, Emily, Rachel for the cross-team RFC. Will ping product for buy-in. :thumbsup:
Rachel: copying PM for capacity flow design.
Emily: one more: let's add a telemetry alert that fires when fallback_rate > 5% for >10m. That will help ops detect regressions.
Samir: noted. I'll add instrumentation and a short runbook step to autorecover where possible.
Jun: Nice. Looks actionable.
Maya: closing the loop here — thanks all.
